```python
import re
import spacy
from collections import Counter

nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

DATE_PATTERNS = [
    r"\b(?:jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec)[a-z]*\s+\d{1,2}\b",
    r"\b\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{2,4}\b",
    r"\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}\s?(?:am|pm)\b",
]

def analyze_text(text):
    doc = nlp(text)
    entities = Counter(ent.label_ for ent in doc.ents)

    date_hits = sum(bool(re.search(p, text, re.I)) for p in DATE_PATTERNS)

    risk = 0
    if entities["GPE"] or entities["LOC"]:
        risk += 2
    if entities["PERSON"]:
        risk += 1
    risk += date_hits

    return {
        "risk_score": risk,
        "entities": dict(entities),
        "date_pattern_hits": date_hits,
    }

sample = "I’m flying to Chicago on 4/18/2025 and will be gone all week."
print(analyze_text(sample))
```

## Example of a safe privacy-audit skeleton

```python
import re
from collections import Counter

# Broad patterns for privacy auditing only
LOCATION_PATTERNS = [
    r"\b(?:in|from|near)\s+[A-Z][a-z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)?\b",
    r"\b(?:NYC|LA|SF|Chicago|Boston|Seattle|Austin)\b",
]

DATE_PATTERNS = [
    r"\b\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{2,4}\b",
    r"\b\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b",
    r"\b(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\s+\d{1,2}\b",
]

TIME_PATTERNS = [
    r"\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}\s?(?:AM|PM|am|pm)?\b",
    r"\b(?:morning|afternoon|evening|tonight|yesterday|today)\b",
]

def scan_text(text):
    findings = Counter()

    for pattern in LOCATION_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pattern, text):
            findings["location"] += 1

    for pattern in DATE_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pattern, text):
            findings["date"] += 1

    for pattern in TIME_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pattern, text):
            findings["time"] += 1

    return findings

def summarize_posts(posts):
    totals = Counter()
    for text in posts:
        totals.update(scan_text(text))
    return totals

# Example usage with placeholder text only
sample_posts = [
    "I moved to Boston in 2023-09-10 and started work at 9:30 AM.",
    "Going to NYC next Friday.",
    "Met someone yesterday evening."
]

results = summarize_posts(sample_posts)
print(results)
```

```python
import re
import json
from collections import Counter

# Simple patterns for privacy review
PATTERNS = {
    "email": re.compile(r"\b[\w\.-]+@[\w\.-]+\.\w+\b"),
    "phone": re.compile(r"\b(?:\+?\d{1,3}[-.\s]?)?(?:\(?\d{3}\)?[-.\s]?)\d{3}[-.\s]?\d{4}\b"),
    "date": re.compile(r"\b(?:\d{1,2}[/-]\d{1,2}[/-]\d{2,4}|\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|"
                       r"(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\s+\d{1,2},\s+\d{4})\b",
                       re.IGNORECASE),
    "time": re.compile(r"\b(?:[01]?\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d(?:\s?[APap][Mm])?\b"),
    "zipcode": re.compile(r"\b\d{5}(?:-\d{4})?\b"),
}

# Very light location indicators (customize for your use case)
LOCATION_HINTS = [
    "street", "st.", "avenue", "ave", "road", "rd.", "blvd", "lane", "ln.",
    "city", "state", "county", "near", "downtown"
]

def detect_sensitive(text):
    hits = []
    lower = text.lower()

    for label, pattern in PATTERNS.items():
        for match in pattern.findall(text):
            hits.append((label, match))

    if any(hint in lower for hint in LOCATION_HINTS):
        hits.append(("location_hint", "possible location reference"))

    return hits

def audit_items(items):
    all_hits = []
    summary = Counter()

    for item in items:
        text = item.get("text", "")
        hits = detect_sensitive(text)
        if hits:
            all_hits.append({
                "id": item.get("id"),
                "text": text[:200],
                "hits": hits
            })
            for label, _ in hits:
                summary[label] += 1

    return all_hits, summary

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Example local input: [{"id":"1","text":"Met at 3:30 PM near Main St."}, ...]
    with open("posts.json", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        items = json.load(f)

    flagged, summary = audit_items(items)

    print("Privacy audit summary:")
    for k, v in summary.items():
        print(f"  {k}: {v}")

    print("\nFlagged items:")
    for item in flagged:
        print(item)
```

This kind of script demonstrates how easily public text can contain:
